correctness.rationale: All parameters \(m\ge3\) and \(\ell\ge3\). Fixing tail increments, the normalized core clique polytope is optimized by strict convexity only at signed binary vertices (with a nonzero coordinate). Squared pairwise-distance domination strictly straightens the tail away from the negative clique value, so every maximizer has the stated form. The remaining exact numerator \(N(B+k)-(A-k)^2\) completes the square at \(c=(m+\ell(\ell+2))/2\); clipping and nearest integer select every optimizer, giving unique boundary, tie, and mixed regimes. The proof verifies strict equality at each step. Standalone code independently enumerates 47 exact small cases and verifies 35,920 quadratic instances; finite checks are not substituted for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The standard lollipop family connects a dense concentration core to a long bottleneck path. Its exact sharp real Lipschitz variance and complete optimizer classification are natural unknown graph concentration data. The new quadratic \(m=\ell(\ell+2)+3\) coexistence threshold distinguishes fully polarized versus genuinely mixed clique extremizers and changes the large-clique structure; the parity correction in the mixing regime is exact. The result excludes the already-covered tail length two and proves a nontrivial two-parameter structural law rather than a numerical sample or a mere substitution.
